children: and Arbitrum’s venture arm Tandem co-led a $5 million seed round for Rialto, an on-chain trading startup that has already processed more than $600 million in volume.
Rialto Emerges From Stealth With Robinhood Backing
Robinhood and Tandem were the only investors in the round, which opened in October 2025 and closed in early 2026, Rialto co-founder Can told The Block.
The deal was structured as equity with token warrants, and Can declined to disclose a valuation or say whether Rialto plans to launch its own token.
Rialto’s team comes mostly from a high-frequency trading background, and Can said that experience is now carrying over to on-chain markets.

"Onchain markets have demonstrated the benefits of transparency and composability, but the next phase requires trading infrastructure that can deliver competitive liquidity and execution at scale," he said.
The platform offers spot crypto trading plus more than 200 Robinhood Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain, tokenized versions of stocks, ETFs and commodities.
Rialto leans on its own market-making technology, which it calls "PropAMM," alongside a router that Can said cut average quote response times from 250 milliseconds to 20 milliseconds.
Rialto’s October trading volume hit $199.3 million, up from $53.4 million in September, while stock token volume jumped 329% to $183.8 million.
Since its public launch in July, the platform has processed more than $600 million combined across its app and Swap API.
Robinhood Chain remains Rialto’s priority, though its Swap API also runs on Arbitrum, and Can said the company has no other blockchain expansion to announce.

Rialto earns revenue from a 5-basis-point trading fee on its app and plans to use the new funding for product development, hiring and growth. Founded in mid-2025, the company has fewer than 10 employees across Europe and Asia.
Robinhood shares trade near $65, down 3.5% on the session, and remain below all four daily EMAs, a sign the stock’s short-term trend is still bearish.

Support sits near $62, then $60, and a break below that zone could extend the decline toward $55. Buyers need to reclaim $68 to $70 to ease the pressure, with $73 and the 20-day EMA at $77.70 standing as the next hurdles on any recovery.
